_comment_family: The 400-weight slanted cut, and the block face of every channel set
in this family. Its partner is open-sans-bolditalic.json, which is
the same slant at 700 and is what a picked word is set in; that
pack's note is the one to read for what the pairing has to survive.
It declares a full name instead of 'Open Sans' because that is what
the file carries as name ID 1, and the Bold Italic carries it too —
two files answering to one family name, separated only by their
subfamily. Asking for the family would let either of them answer, and
a block that came back bold, or a picked word that came back at 400,
is not a variation on the design: it is the highlight disappearing
into the text. So the full name (ID 4) is what gets declared, the
same way telegraf-ultralight declares 'Telegraf UltraLight' rather
than 'Telegraf'. Two distinct family names is also what lets one
channel be set in both at once, because fontguard keys its check by
family and each cut is then verified in its own right.
It matters more here than it does for the faces this folder invented
a name for, because Open Sans is one a Windows machine may genuinely
already carry — from a Google Fonts install, or dragged in by another
application. A pack declaring the bare family would be handing the
local() route a name any cut of that family can answer to.
Weight 400, because that is what the cut is: this family's italic
is a true drawn italic and not a heavier weight, and asking for
anything else invites a browser to synthesise a difference the file
does not have.
Registered at style normal on purpose, the same way hanken-grotesk-
italic and rift are. The slant is drawn into the letterforms; the
file's own fsSelection says italic, but declaring the FACE italic here
as well would leave the canvas — which asks for normal — either
missing it or being handed a synthetic oblique of something else.
Normal means 'this file, as drawn'.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the PostScript name and is also what the installer
registers the face under; the second is the Windows full name. Both
name this one cut rather than the family, so a machine answering to
either is answering with this file. 'Open Sans' on its own is
deliberately absent: it is the name the Bold Italic answers to as
well, which is the whole of the reason this pack names a cut.
_comment_stack: A 400-weight humanist sans falls back to the nearest weight the
machine is certain to have, not to Impact — most of the faces in this
folder fall back through Impact and Arial Black because most of them
are heavy display cuts, and this is not one.
